verdict_reason: THE SOLE BLOCKER I NAMED LAST ROUND IS CLOSED AND I VERIFIED IT WITH THE COUNTEREXAMPLE THAT MOTIVATED IT, NOT WITH THE DOCSTRING. The headline is now `float(np.mean(margin_tokens))`, so it is a mean of per-token margins over one row set instead of a difference of two means over different row sets. On WikiText it is bit-identical to the old form -- gpt2 +0.01154154, distilgpt2 +0.01553551, pythia-70m +0.00574500, agreeing with (mean raw - mean control) to 6.915e-13 / 1.092e-12 / 1.139e-12 -- and on the corpus that exposed the bug it no longer moves: adding 50 two-token documents (n_lab = 1, so they contribute a raw cosine but no control) to a 50-document gpt2 corpus leaves the headline bit-identical at +0.01111735 while the OLD formula drifts to +0.01078997 (-2.95%) with `_meta_prediction_alignment_freq_baseline` unchanged at -0.13208955. `prediction_alignment_std` (0.03003317) is now over the same rows as the mean. The control itself I re-verified as an invariant rather than a number: the Sattolo loop (j drawn from [0, i-1]) yields a single cycle, the repair pass swaps two entries of the ORDER array so permutation-ness survives by construction, and its third guard `_lab_list[_order[_i]] != _lab_list[_k]` is what prevents a swap from re-creating an index fixed point -- measured over 12,795 / 12,795 / 13,086 positions on gpt2 / distilgpt2 / pythia-70m: 0 invalid permutations, 0 index fixed points, 0 residual label collisions. Hidden-state/label alignment in collect_prediction_stats is h[:, :-1] against input_ids[:, 1:], which is correct. Nothing that remains changes a value on the paper-defined domain; the outstanding items are a docstring over-claim, a missing diagnostic and a corner-case fallback, all recorded below.
comparable_reason: Much better than the raw cosine it replaced: the promoted column spans 0.005745-0.015536 across the three models where the raw cosine spans 1.043 (gpt2 -0.120083, distilgpt2 -0.103280, pythia-70m +0.923067), and the anisotropy readout that used to dominate is behind `_meta_`. Two caveats, both re-measured. First, no uncertainty is reported for a headline of magnitude ~0.006-0.016 whose per-token dispersion is 2-3x the mean (gpt2 0.029203 against 0.011542; distilgpt2 0.024296 against 0.015536; pythia-70m 0.018762 against 0.005745), so pythia-70m's +0.005745 cannot be distinguished from zero as reported. Second, `prediction_alignment_margin_uniform` is emitted unprefixed alongside the headline and disagrees with it in SIGN on gpt2 (-0.00768113 against +0.01154154) while agreeing on distilgpt2 (+0.01177329) and pythia-70m (+0.00081214), so two feature columns answer the same question oppositely on one of three models.
normalized_ok_reason: The frequency-matched control does exactly what it is defined to do, and the row-set fix makes the reported mean the mean of the very margins the control produces. Multiset equality of control and true labels holds by construction (the control is an index permutation applied to the label list) and I confirmed 0 invalid permutations and 0 index fixed points on all 300 real documents; residual label collisions are 0 of 12,795 (gpt2), 0 of 12,795 (distilgpt2) and 0 of 13,086 (pythia-70m), so the emitted margin equals a strictly-non-target margin exactly on this corpus. The within-document scope is stated in the class docstring. The uniform control is a genuine second baseline and correctly shows that the raw cosine carries almost no target information (gpt2 raw -0.120083 against a uniform baseline -0.112402; pythia-70m +0.923067 against +0.922255).

confounds_reason: The confounded column is no longer the headline. defects: THE CLASS DOCSTRING STATES A CORPUS PROPERTY AS AN ESTIMATOR PROPERTY, AND THE TASK EMITS NO DIAGNOSTIC TO CHECK IT. 'Residual label collisions ... are **0.000%** after the repair pass' is true on WikiText (0 of 12,795 / 12,795 / 13,086) and false in general, because a frequency-matched control CANNOT avoid a collision when the document's labels repeat. On a 20-document corpus of ' the' x 20 the collision rate is 380/380 = 100.00% and the emitted `prediction_alignment_mean` is exactly 0.0 with `prediction_alignment_std` exactly 0.0 -- the margin collapses, correctly by definition, but silently. The collision rate is measured nowhere and emitted nowhere, so the degradation is invisible to a consumer. Fix: emit `_meta_prediction_alignment_control_collision_rate` and soften the docstring to 'measured 0.000% on WikiText'.

THE FALLBACK PATH SILENTLY CHANGES THE ESTIMAND OF AN UNPREFIXED FEATURE COLUMN. If no document has n_lab > 1, `prediction_alignment_mean` becomes the RAW cosine. Measured on a 50-document all-two-token gpt2 corpus: -0.16653611, against +0.01111735 on WikiText -- opposite sign, 15x magnitude, same column name. The only signal is `_meta_prediction_alignment_uncorrected: True`, which a feature matrix filtered by is_feature() never sees. Fix: emit NaN, or a separately named key.

No uncertainty is reported for a headline of 0.005745-0.015536 whose per-token dispersion is 0.018762-0.029203, i.e. 2-3x the mean. A per-document bootstrap over the 100 documents costs nothing and is the difference between pythia-70m's +0.005745 being a finding and being noise.
`prediction_alignment_margin_uniform` and `prediction_alignment_mean` are both unprefixed features and disagree in sign on gpt2 (-0.00768113 vs +0.01154154).

PERFORMANCE, not correctness: one torch.randint call per position (about 12,800 CPU RNG calls per model at the shipped num_samples) plus an O(n^2) repair pass per document. One vectorised numpy Sattolo pass is identical in distribution and orders of magnitude cheaper.
The `_mean - _bf` fallback inside `if baseline_freq:` is now dead code -- baseline_freq and margin_tokens are appended together, so margin_tokens is non-empty whenever baseline_freq is.
